efficacy.confidence_note: CSR synopsis CL004_140 v1.0 (17 Mar 2011), posted to EU CTR 2022-03-01, read in full via pdftotext. The synopsis does not name the variant; the ClinicalTrials.gov record (NCT01028963) does not mention the stratification at all.
efficacy.judgement: First use of a human genetic stratifier for the class: the sponsor randomised within strata of MCP-1 polymorphism status, presumably the CCL2 -2518A/G promoter variant whose G allele lowers plasma MCP-1 and T2D prevalence (Simeoni 2004, doi:10.1007/s00125-004-1494-4). Patient-level, because the question is whether genotype predicts response to CCX140-B, not whether the class works. Opened at the trial's start (29 Jan 2010) with the 2022 registry posting as proxy source; product_in_model true because the member drug was dosed to the genotyped patients.

efficacy.note: CCX140-B 4-week T2D trial (CL004_140, Jan-Nov 2010) randomised patients within strata of MCP-1 polymorphism status; genotype-by-response was a stated objective.
efficacy.short: Trial stratified by MCP-1 genotype; no result yet
efficacy.quote: Eligible subjects were stratified based on MCP-1 polymorphism status as well as gender.

efficacy.confidence_note: The synopsis (full read) reports FPG, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, insulin, OGTT, adiponectin, MCP-1 and hsCRP by arm and nothing by genotype. Whether the EASD 2011 presentation or Hanefeld 2012 J Diabetes Metab (not locatable in PubMed or at OMICS) reported the genotype analysis could not be checked; the 15 Sep 2011 press release does not mention it.
efficacy.judgement: Stays untested: the sponsor stated the genotype-by-response objective and never published its result anywhere found, so there is no comparison to score. Not trial_unreported, because the trial itself is reported at tier 3; only the stratifier analysis is missing. An unreported stratifier is not a contra. Dated 2022, the first time the objective and the stratification were public.

considered_not_added: Sullivan 2013 Metabolism (doi:10.1016/j.metabol.2013.06.008, PMID 23953944, epub 2013-08-15; mouse-active analogue of CCX140-B in DIO and db/db mice): the same system as the draft's dio-dbdb-mouse-ccr2-antagonist track, so no new model_id. For the main draft: it is the member's own model and should be the model_src of the CCX140-B pairing; its abstract states the comparison ('These mechanisms may contribute to the promising anti-diabetic effects seen in humans with at least one CCR2 antagonist'), which makes that pairing sponsor-stated.

de Zeeuw 2015 Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol (doi:10.1016/S2213-8587(15)00261-2, PMID 26268910; 52-week CCX140-B 5/10 mg in T2D with nephropathy, NCT01447147): patient side only, HbA1c a secondary; belongs in patient_trials of the existing mouse track, not a model system.
Ccr2-/- knockout mice (Weisberg 2006): already carried inside the draft's DIO track quote; not a separate track.

Propagermanium in high-fat-fed C57BL/6 mice (Tamura 2010, PMID 20179360; Mulder 2017, PMID 28076416) and alpha-mangostin (Kim 2017, PMID 28598982): the same DIO system with non-member CCR2 inhibitors; no patient comparison and nothing the Weisberg track does not already say.
RO5234444 in uninephrectomised db/db mice (Sayyed 2011 Kidney Int, PMID 21508925): diabetic-nephropathy readouts with a non-member antagonist; not T2D glycaemia, no patient comparison.

hCCR2 knock-in mouse for the BMS series (Yang 2021, PMID 34141082: monocyte migration and MS models for BMS-753426; Yang 2019, PMID 30891130: BMS-741672 discovery): no T2D model and no patient comparison; the BMS-741672 T2D trial NCT00699790 was never reported, so there is nothing to pair.

Human ex-vivo whole-blood CCR2 occupancy / chemotaxis PD assays in volunteers: no member publication found (the only PD hit, Hara 2013 PMID 23564379, is in-vitro human fibrocytes with no drug-trial comparison).

In-silico / PK-PD dose model: the CL004_140 synopsis says a PK/PD relationship 'was to be evaluated, if possible' and parks the PK in an unposted appendix; no published model for any member, so no track.

MCP-1 -2518A/G population genetics as a class-level human_genetic track (Simeoni 2004, PMID 15349727: G allele lowers MCP-1, OR 0.80 for T2D; Kaur 2009, PMID 19450143: opposite direction for metabolic syndrome): a ligand-level association never set beside a member trial by any source and internally inconsistent; recorded as the rationale inside the patient-level track rather than opened as its own class-level track.
JNJ-41443532 preclinical model: no model paper found under the drug name (PubMed returns only Di Prospero 2014), so nothing beyond the draft's existing track.
Retracted JPET 2012 CCX140-B characterisation (PMID 22378937): not used, as in the draft.
